items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: Bucky, the gentleman, when Bucky was on the road with Stephane Grappelli, he brought this case of music to him, so Bucky brought it back to me and we looked at it

ctx.x: I don’t mean to keep bringing up Manny again, but he talked about that too, about trying to write for strings and make them swing, and he basically said don’t bother.

No. You’re wasting your time. I had a wonderful experience — Bucky found, Bucky Pizzarelli found a gentleman who is now 96 years old or something, a black violinist from the south, I think he lived in Carolina or someplace. And Paul Whiteman had heard him play, and Paul Whiteman was a genius businessman. And he heard him play and he called in one of his myriad arrangers who sat at his elbow, and they wrote arrangements on standards for four violins, traps, utility percussion, bass — we can’t tell, it’s probably…
How much time do you get to create an album with the New York Pops in the studio?
